source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
QTS Piscataway Data Center in Piscataway, New Jersey, publishes 65 MW of IT capacity, operated by Quality Technology Services.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 6500 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 1625 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

QTS Piscataway Data Center holds 1 published certification: LEED (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

New Jersey has 4 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 3 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 94 MW. QTS Piscataway Data Center contributes 65 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
